hero.headline: Port St. Lucie teen to serve as flag bearer at FIFA World Cup finals
hero.body:
Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce with a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. He will serve as one of 12 club members from across the country selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19. The surprise came courtesy of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and their partnership with the Coca-Cola Company. When the box containing the news was walked into the room surrounded by fellow club members, Rosario Liz's reaction was immediate. "This is crazy. I mean, this is so insane," Rosario Liz said. Along with the trip, he also received official gear inside the box.

Rosario Liz had already been juggling a packed summer, preparing for move-in at the University of Florida and an internship, but said the World Cup had been on his mind. "My time is really being taken up by the World Cup right now, forcing my parents to watch every game," Rosario Liz said. He credited the Boys & Girls Club with shaping who he has become as a leader. "The club really helped me to find what my leadership style was going to be, and really redefined what my definition of leadership was," Rosario Liz said. "The Boys & Girls Clubs has been my everything," he said. He closed with a message for younger members: "Please stay with your Boys & Girls Clubs, because one day I want to see each and every one of you in the same position that I am in right now."

cards.headline: St. Lucie County woman accused of using vehicle to assault three people
cards.body:
Tioniea Hines, 22, is being held in the St. Lucie County Jail on $75,000 bond after being accused of using her vehicle as a weapon in an assault involving three people. She faces three counts of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon.

The charges stem from an incident in which Hines allegedly used her vehicle to attack three individuals. Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon is a felony offense in Florida, carrying significant prison time if convicted.

Hines remains in custody at the St. Lucie County Jail. The bond was set at $75,000 for the three counts she faces.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office handled the arrest. Court records show Hines was booked into the jail on the three felony charges.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Three-Game Skid With 4-1 Win Over Jupiter
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed o
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed only minutes to take control. The first three batters of the game all reached and scored before an out was recorded. Elian Peña opened with a single, Mike Tauchman doubled him home, and Trey Snyder followed with a two-run homer off Walin Castillo for a 3-0 lead.

Julio Zayas added a solo shot with two outs in the third to push the margin to 4-0.

That was more than enough for starter Emilio Obispo, who threw five shutout innings and lowered his season ERA to 1.82. He scattered four singles, walked three and struck out six to earn his fourth win of the year.

Obispo worked out of trouble when it mattered. He struck out Josh Hogue to strand the bases loaded in the third, induced a double play to end the fourth, and retired the side in order in the fifth to finish his outing.

Jupiter loaded the bases against Calvin Ziegler in the sixth. Ziegler struck out Jake McCutheon for the second out before Zack Mack entered and ended the threat with a popout. Mack went 2.1 innings and allowed one unearned run, which came in the eighth when Andres Valor stole third and scored on a throwing error.

Elwis Mijares closed it out with a 1-2-3 ninth on 11 pitches for his second save.

Tauchman, rehabbing a torn meniscus, went 1 for 3 with the double, an RBI and a run while playing six innings in left field in his first rehab game with St. Lucie. Snyder led the offense at 2 for 4 with the homer and two RBI.

The Mets (5-13, 38-46) and Hammerheads (8-12, 45-41) close their six-game series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. A win would give St. Lucie its first 3-3 series split of 2026. First pitch is 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida home insurance market improves as more carriers return to state
cards.teaser: Florida's troubled home insurance market shows signs of recovery with more insurers returning to the state and some rates declining.
cards.body:
Florida's home insurance market shows signs of improvement as more insurers return and some rates decline, according to recent reports. The development marks a potential shift in a market that has faced significant challenges in recent years, particularly following major hurricane damage.

The return of additional insurance carriers to Florida could provide homeowners with more coverage options after years of market instability. Some insurers had previously left the state or stopped writing new policies due to hurricane risk and financial losses. The improvements come as the state continues working to stabilize its property insurance sector through regulatory changes and market adjustments.

The recovery in Florida's insurance market represents a significant development for a state that has struggled with coverage availability and affordability. Homeowners have faced limited options as carriers withdrew from the market or restricted new policy writing in response to catastrophic hurricane losses. The return of more insurance companies suggests growing confidence in the state's efforts to address the underlying issues that drove insurers away.

While the market shows signs of stabilization, Florida homeowners continue to face challenges related to hurricane exposure and insurance costs. The state's vulnerability to tropical storms and hurricanes remains a fundamental concern for insurers evaluating their risk exposure. However, the willingness of carriers to return to the Florida market indicates potential progress in creating conditions that allow insurers to operate profitably while providing necessary coverage to residents in hurricane-prone areas.

cards.headline: Indian River County research highlights district strategy amid school choice expansion
cards.teaser: A new case study examines how Indian River County schools are responding to enrollment challenges as school choice options expand.
cards.body:
New research has focused on Indian River County schools and the district's approach to reversing enrollment declines in the expanding school choice era. The case study explores strategies the district is implementing to attract and retain students.

Indian River County schools face enrollment challenges as families have more educational options through charter schools, vouchers, and other school choice programs. The research documents how district officials are working to compete in this changed landscape.

The case study provides insight into the specific tactics Indian River County is employing to stabilize and grow enrollment. School choice expansion has created competitive pressure on traditional public school districts across Florida, making enrollment management a priority for district leadership.

District administrators are responding to the competitive environment created by increased educational alternatives available to families. The research examines the approaches being taken to address declining student numbers as more parents choose options outside traditional public schools.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie soccer stadium groundbreaking set for November with 6,000-seat design
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie SC released new renderings of its 6,000-seat stadium this week, with groundbreaking anticipated in November at the Walton & One development along U.S. 1 and Walton Road.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie SC released new renderings this week of its 6,000-seat stadium, with groundbreaking anticipated in November. The stadium will be built at the Walton & One development, a 46-acre mixed-use redevelopment project located along U.S. 1 and Walton Road. The club's inaugural season begins in 2027, and the future stadium is scheduled to open in early 2028.

The team has not announced where they plan to play next year while the facility is under construction. The club posted Thursday on social media that their home venue will be a place where soccer, community, and unforgettable moments will come together. The club said the 6,000-seat venue will have the flexibility to grow in capacity and serve as a year-round gathering place for matchdays, concerts, festivals, and community events.

Port St. Lucie resident Zach Woods said there is nothing to do in Port St. Lucie for the most part and the stadium may be the first cool thing the city has brought. Barber Focus Sanders at Sapps Barbershop said the stadium offers more business because it will bring more people, including those from out of town. The city said the stadium is an $80 million economic investment, and no taxpayer money will be used for its construction. The city was awarded a United Soccer League League One Team last October, and city council members unanimously approved both the funding and operating agreements.

cards.headline: Czech player Linda Noskova wins Wimbledon singles title
cards.teaser: Linda Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday.
cards.body:
The 21-year-old Noskova claimed her first Grand Slam trophy at Wimbledon. She became the third Czech woman in four years to win the grass-court major, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024.

Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, was in attendance, as was Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club. Navratilova looked on from the Royal Box, where she was seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales, who was due to present the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova. Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth.

hero.headline: Karolina Muchova defeats Coco Gauff to reach Wimbledon final
hero.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker.
hero.body:
The ninth-ranked Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker. Muchova became the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal next on Centre Court. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, who was runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, who won the championship in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, who won the championship in 2024.

For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

cards.headline: Park Vista football team aims for state playoffs after strong 2025 finish
cards.teaser: Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026.
cards.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The team struggled to find its footing early in 2025 but finished strong, winning four of its last five games. "Felt good throughout the second half of that season," senior Harris Bender said. "We're just working towards being able to carry that through the whole season, like you said, and we have all the pieces in place now, it's just about executing." The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017.

Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna emphasized a measured approach to reaching those goals. "We got to take it one game at a time," Hanna said. "We can't look past anyone. We got to handle business weekly and if we do that, do our job, that'll get us in the playoffs." Senior Erik Lee said the team has the necessary talent but must put in the work. "Coming in, I feel like we got the guys that we need to get it done," Lee said. "But also, we got to put the work in to get there as well." Senior Justice Jones expressed confidence about the upcoming season. Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August.

hero.headline: Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as Treasure Coast shoppers seek relief from rising grocery costs
hero.teaser: A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to customers already facing tight budgets. The opening comes
hero.body:
A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to customers already facing tight budgets. The opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year, prompting more households to adjust their purchasing decisions based on price rather than preference. For shoppers looking to stretch their dollars, the discount grocer offers an alternative to traditional supermarkets at a time when food costs continue to climb.

Customers Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited an affordable option like the new Aldi store is now open close to their home. Cheryl said grocery prices are getting expensive and are starting to change the way she shops. "They're the type of people who never used to look at prices, but now she will go with what's on sale instead of just with what they want, and they never used to do that," she said. The changing shopping habits reflect a broader trend as more households look for ways to manage rising food costs.

Price movements in key grocery categories show a mixed picture for consumers. Egg prices are dropping, and beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1% from April to May, and chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1%. Despite some declining categories, the overall trajectory points to continued upward pressure on grocery bills.

Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon. "Prices are gonna stay inflated and are not gonna go down," they said, adding they would be willing to bet on that. Still, they said stores like Aldi, which often have lower prices than other stores, can make a difference for everyday shoppers. "Having stuff like this for the average person is extremely beneficial because there's nobody who isn't feeling the price increase," they said. The new location gives Treasure Coast residents another option for managing household budgets as inflation continues to impact the cost of food.

hero.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with panoramic views
hero.teaser: Built in 1860, the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The 105-step climb to the top rewards visitors with breathtaking views of the Atlantic Ocean, Jupiter Inlet, and Loxahatchee and Indian rivers.
hero.body:
Built in 1860, the Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The striking red brick tower rises high above the inlet, continuing to serve as both a historic landmark and an active attraction for visitors seeking to experience its rich history and spectacular views from the top.

The 105-step climb to the top follows a narrow spiral staircase that lighthouse keepers once climbed night after night to maintain the powerful Fresnel lens that shone for mariners navigating the waters below. Each step connects modern visitors to the keepers who dedicated their lives to guiding ships safely along Florida's treacherous coastline. The journey upward offers a glimpse into the daily routine of those who maintained this vital navigational aid through the decades, carrying the weight of history with every footfall.

Reaching the gallery at the top rewards visitors with breathtaking panoramic views in every direction. The Atlantic Ocean stretches endlessly to the east, while the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet meet the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers below. Boats glide through the channel as the sea breeze sweeps across the observation deck, making even warm Florida mornings feel comfortable. The vantage point provides a unique perspective on the surrounding waterways and coastline that mariners have relied upon for over a century and a half.

After descending from the tower, visitors can explore the museum grounds and restored historic buildings that tell the story of the lighthouse's fascinating past. The exhibits cover the lighthouse's construction before the Civil War, a tumultuous period in American history when this beacon first began its service. The displays also detail the lighthouse's years as an active Coast Guard station, highlighting the evolution of lighthouse keeping and maritime safety over the generations. The combination of climbing the working lighthouse and exploring the museum grounds offers a comprehensive look at how this structure has served the Florida coast for more than 165 years, making it both an educational experience and a memorable visit for anyone interested in maritime history or seeking the spectacular views from the top of the red brick tower.
